newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia faction starts handing over weapons.
newsitem.headline: Liberia faction starts handing over weapons.

text.p: Fighters loyal to Liberian faction leader Alhaji Kromah handed over some of their weapons to West African peacekeepers on Saturday, in a further step towards ending more than six years of civil war.

Witnesses said the newly installed head of Liberia's transitional ruling State Council, Ruth Perry, attended the ceremony in Kromah's stronghold in this north western town along with General Victor Malu, head of the Nigerian-led peacekeepers.
"The exercise will continue until we are totally disarmed," Kromah said.
Kromah is a State Council vice-chairman. His ULIMO-K faction was at the heart of fighting that killed hundreds of people in Liberia's capital Monrovia in April and May.
His Mandingo fighters fought alongside fellow State Council vice-chairman Charles Taylor's men against an alliance from the Krahn ethnic group, which ruled Liberia during the 1980s.
Taylor and his supporters launched the civil war in late 1989 in Liberia, which was founded by freed American slaves in 1847. The war has killed well over 150,000 people.

West African leaders, frustrated by the collapse of a dozen peace deals, rallied Liberia's warlords in August round a revamped peace deal which envisages a truce, disarmament by January and elections by May.
They have threatened individual sanctions against any faction leader who derails the peace process.
